claims: A reduced-cost potential certificate proves every closed walk has non-negative total weight.
Potential differences telescope, so certificate soundness reduces to non-negativity of reduced path weights.
The same certificate gives a lower bound for any open path: path weight is at least final potential minus initial potential.
Path weights are additive in edge weights and can be packaged as an AddMonoidHom.
Valid certificates compose under edge-weight addition by adding their potentials.
A negative cycle is an explicit obstruction to any valid potential certificate.
If both a weight function and its negation admit certificates, the weight function is an exact coboundary and every cycle has zero circulation.
Single-edge updates preserve a certificate when the updated edge still satisfies the reduced-cost condition.
proof_method: integer linear arithmetic over reduced costs
contrapositive use of certificate soundness for negative-cycle exclusion

boundaries: The graph model is represented by total functions over natural-number vertices, not by a finite edge-set structure.
The certificate checks reduced costs universally over vertex pairs; a runtime finite graph must provide a faithful finite-domain checker or an equivalent specialization.
These proofs establish potential-certificate soundness, not route optimality, oracle freshness, authorization, or runtime gas/complexity bounds.
